text.en:
A lift in a building goes up to floors 1, 2, 3 and down to basement levels −1 and −2. Karan was on floor 2 and went down 5 floors.
"Where am I?" he asked. His sister drew a number line. "At −3, in the basement."

Integers are the whole numbers and their negatives: ..., −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ... On the number line numbers to the right are bigger. Adding a positive number moves to the right and adding a negative number moves to the left.
Adding integers: with the same signs add the numbers and keep the sign, so (−3) + (−4) = −7. With different signs subtract the smaller from the larger and keep the sign of the larger: 5 + (−8) = −3.
Subtracting an integer is the same as adding its opposite: 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8 and 2 − 6 = 2 + (−6) = −4. The opposite of a number has the same size but the other sign.
Integers are whole numbers and their negatives. On the number line right means bigger.
To add integers with the same sign, add the numbers and keep the sign.
With different signs, subtract the smaller from the larger and keep the sign of the larger.
Subtracting an integer is adding its opposite.
Subtracting an integer means adding its opposite.

why.en: On the number line we move right.

prompt.en: A friend says (−3) + (−4) = 1. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: Both numbers are negative, so we add 3 and 4 to get 7 and keep the negative sign.

points.en: Same signs: add and keep the sign.
Different signs: subtract and keep the sign of the larger.
